Evaluate classification accuracy, consistency and conditional precision

Source: R/api-classification.R
classification_table.Rd

Evaluate a fixed future rating plan under an ordinary RSM/PCM calibration. Lee-style recursion gives the exact finite summed-score distribution; the Rudner comparison uses a normal approximation to an ML ability estimate.

Usage

classification_table(
  fit,
  rating_plan,
  cut_scores,
  score_cuts,
  theta,
  theta_weights = NULL,
  operational_cuts = cut_scores,
  facets = NULL,
  readiness_policy = c("error", "review")
)

Arguments

fit

A native ordinary RSM/PCM fit_mfrm() result (MML or JML), without interactions, random effects or a JML correction.

rating_plan

Data frame with one row per future rating and exactly the calibrated facet identifier columns. All levels must be known. Duplicate complete facet cells, missing identifiers, score columns and observation weights are not supported. Each row contributes one rating.

cut_scores

Finite, strictly increasing true-ability category cuts on the calibration scale. Optional names label the cuts.

score_cuts

Nondecreasing integer cuts on the sum of model category indices, each rating scored 0, ..., K-1. One cut per cut_scores. Values from zero through the maximum possible sum plus one are allowed. Repeated cuts retain empty categories; zero and maximum-plus-one retain unreachable edge categories. These are explicit operational decisions, not automatically rounded expected scores or sums of original labels.

theta

Finite numeric vector of true-ability points to evaluate. Supply a grid around the cuts to inspect conditional precision there. Fitted EAPs are not automatically substituted for true abilities.

theta_weights

Optional nonnegative population point/quadrature weights corresponding to theta, with at least one positive entry. Weights are normalized and retained. Density values alone are generally insufficient on an unequally spaced grid. No default population is used.

operational_cuts

Strictly increasing ability-estimate decision cuts for the Rudner approximation, one per true cut. Defaults to cut_scores.

facets

Optional character vector mapping calibrated facet names to rating_plan columns, as in predict_mfrm_units().

readiness_policy

"error" requires a ready source calibration. "review" permits a nonready but valid source and retains its assessment in source; it does not establish statistical adequacy. Invalid retained parameters cannot be overridden.

Value

A plain list. table contains conditional indices, expected sum, information, SEM and availability for each point/method. SourceStatus in table, probabilities, scores, cuts, marginal and classification_matrix preserves the separate calibration assessment, including in CSV exports. Status, where present, describes numerical availability; an available row with SourceStatus = "review_only" still needs source review. Inspect source$reason_codes for the reasons. probabilities contains operational category probabilities; scores contains the exact summed-score probability mass. cuts reports both cut scales and SEM at true and operational ability cuts. marginal and classification_matrix are empty unless population weights are supplied. Any unavailable point with positive weight makes its method's marginal results unavailable; such points are never dropped or renormalized away. population retains input points and raw/normalized weights. rating_plan, calibration (offsets, cumulative thresholds and category map), source, settings and notes retain the calculation's conditions. A source review status applies to the entire result, including numerically available rows. Save with base::saveRDS() or export tables with utils::write.csv(). A table CSV alone does not retain the plan, cut definitions, population distribution and notes; keep the full result for reproducible reuse. Reading saved output does not refit or recalculate anything.

Details

Both methods are returned. For an operational decision based on the declared category-score sum, report the lee_sum row. For a decision based on an ML ability estimate, rudner_normal is an approximate comparison, subject to the limitations below. It does not evaluate an EAP/MAP decision rule. The rows need not describe the same decision; compare their accuracy as competing calculations only after matching the actual operational rules. Status = "available" means the calculation succeeded, not that the normal approximation or the fitted model is accurate for the intended population.

Categories are numbered from 1. Values equal to a cut enter the higher category: lower endpoints are inclusive, upper endpoints exclusive. The top category includes the maximum possible sum. True categories use cut_scores; operational categories use score_cuts for lee_sum and operational_cuts for rudner_normal. These can describe different rules. Expected sums at ability cuts are reported for inspection, never rounded into a decision rule. In an ordinary fixed-plan Rasch model the ML score equation is S = E(S | theta). A matched sum cut therefore requires the actual ML decision mapping, including ties and extreme-score policy. EAP/MAP decisions do not automatically share that mapping.

With conditional operational category probabilities p[h] and true category H(theta), accuracy is p[H(theta)]; consistency is sum(p^2). Consistency concerns two conditionally independent repetitions with the same calibrated plan. Overclassification and underclassification sum probabilities above and below the true category. Population versions are weighted averages over the supplied true-ability distribution. The joint matrix contains population joint probabilities, not row-normalized error rates. Accuracy need not exceed consistency in a multicategory decision. With two categories, marginal overclassification is the joint probability of a true fail and an observed pass; underclassification is the joint probability of a true pass and an observed fail. Divide each by its true category's population probability for the error rate conditional on that category. A zero denominator makes that conditional rate undefined. Conditioning instead on the observed pass/fail category uses its column sum in the joint matrix and answers how often that reported decision is wrong.

Information sums conditional category-score variances over the plan. SEM = 1/sqrt(Information) is a conditional ability-scale SEM with calibration fixed, not a posterior SD, sum-score SEM or an SE propagating facet estimation uncertainty. rudner_normal assumes an ML estimator's sampling distribution is normal with mean theta and this SEM. Short plans, extremes, estimator bias and model misfit can invalidate that approximation. Zero numerical information gives infinite SEM and makes Rudner results unavailable; Lee probabilities can remain available. Arithmetic overflow or unresolved probability mass causes an error. Narrow normal-probability bands use direct integration when subtraction of cumulative probabilities would lose precision. Finite precision does not guarantee relative accuracy in vanishing tails.

Local independence is assumed even when rows share a task or rater. Calibration, cuts and the plan are held fixed. There is no uncertainty interval, quality threshold, automatic cut selection, random-rater/task generalization, retake policy, or propagation of calibration/population estimation error. Model-based accuracy is not observed reference agreement. This is also distinct from posterior ability-band probabilities in predict_mfrm_units(). Passing calibration checks does not validate the future plan or the normal approximation.

References

Rudner, L. M. (2001). Computing the expected proportions of misclassified examinees. Practical Assessment, Research, and Evaluation, 7, Article 14. doi:10.7275/an9m-2035 .

Rudner, L. M. (2005). Expected classification accuracy. Practical Assessment, Research, and Evaluation, 10, Article 13. doi:10.7275/56a5-6b14 .

Lee, W.-C. (2010). Classification consistency and accuracy for complex assessments using item response theory. Journal of Educational Measurement, 47(1), 1-17. doi:10.1111/j.1745-3984.2009.00096.x .

Wyse, A. E., & Hao, S. (2012). An evaluation of item response theory classification accuracy and consistency indices. Applied Psychological Measurement, 36(7), 602-624. doi:10.1177/0146621612451522 .

Lathrop, Q. N., & Cheng, Y. (2013). Two approaches to estimation of classification accuracy rate under item response theory. Applied Psychological Measurement, 37(3), 226-241. doi:10.1177/0146621612471888 .

See also

predict_mfrm_units(), score_comparison_table()

Examples

ratings <- load_mfrmr_data("example_operational")
fit <- fit_mfrm(ratings, person = "Person", facets = c("Rater", "Criterion"),
  score = "Score", method = "MML", model = "RSM",
  rating_min = 1, rating_max = 4, category_policy = "preserve")
# The planned roster includes the intended ratings even if scores are missing.
data("mfrmr_example_operational_design", package = "mfrmr")
rating_plan <- subset(mfrmr_example_operational_design, Person == "P001",
  select = c("Rater", "Criterion"))
rating_plan # Six ratings: two raters, each scoring three criteria.
#>   Rater    Criterion
#> 1   R01      Content
#> 2   R01     Language
#> 3   R01 Organization
#> 4   R02      Content
#> 5   R02     Language
#> 6   R02 Organization
# Illustrative rules: ability at least 0 logits; original-score sum at least 18.
# score_cuts uses 0:3 category indices, not the original 1:4 score labels:
# subtract 1 for each of the six ratings, so 18 - 6 = 12.
# These are different decision rules, not automatically equivalent cutoffs.
result <- classification_table(fit, rating_plan,
  cut_scores = 0, score_cuts = 12, theta = c(-0.5, 0, 0.5))
result$table
#>   Point Theta TrueCategory        Method  Accuracy Consistency
#> 1     1  -0.5            1       lee_sum 0.9033270   0.8253454
#> 2     1  -0.5            1 rudner_normal 0.8505279   0.7457396
#> 3     2   0.0            2       lee_sum 0.4008877   0.5196465
#> 4     2   0.0            2 rudner_normal 0.5000000   0.5000000
#> 5     3   0.5            2       lee_sum 0.7790621   0.6557513
#> 6     3   0.5            2 rudner_normal 0.8308507   0.7189244
#>   Overclassification Underclassification ExpectedSum Information       SEM
#> 1         0.09667296           0.0000000    8.798214    4.315591 0.4813709
#> 2         0.14947214           0.0000000    8.798214    4.315591 0.4813709
#> 3         0.00000000           0.5991123   10.955735    4.229732 0.4862320
#> 4         0.00000000           0.5000000   10.955735    4.229732 0.4862320
#> 5         0.00000000           0.2209379   12.947095    3.667473 0.5221755
#> 6         0.00000000           0.1691493   12.947095    3.667473 0.5221755
#>      Status SourceStatus
#> 1 available        ready
#> 2 available        ready
#> 3 available        ready
#> 4 available        ready
#> 5 available        ready
#> 6 available        ready
result$cuts
#>    Cut TrueCut OperationalAbilityCut ScoreCut ExpectedSumAtTrueCut
#> 1 Cut1       0                     0       12             10.95574
#>   InformationAtTrueCut SEMAtTrueCut ExpectedSumAtOperationalCut
#> 1             4.229732     0.486232                    10.95574
#>   InformationAtOperationalCut SEMAtOperationalCut SourceStatus
#> 1                    4.229732            0.486232        ready
result$settings$calibration # These probabilities hold calibration fixed.
#> [1] "fixed_point_estimates"
# No population average is inferred from this three-point inspection grid.
